title: Kahani
context: Karya Learn's financial-literacy curriculum — nine story-based chapters written by hand in the Sabido dramatized-storytelling method — worked, but every chapter had to be researched and written manually. Kahani (Hindi for "story") asks whether that same kind of story-based curriculum can be generated by an LLM pipeline instead, starting from real source material rather than a person's manual draft.
question: Can a multi-agent LLM pipeline generate financial-literacy curricula, in narrative/story form, that are as accurate and audience-appropriate as a human-authored one?
methodology: A chain of GPT-4o agents: a curriculum-generation agent drafts a 10-module curriculum from real source material (grounded in the Ujjivan Diksha financial-literacy program, with brand references stripped out), a human-feedback step, an evaluation agent that checks the draft against target-audience appropriateness and factual accuracy to the source, and a final agent that restructures the approved curriculum into the same dramatized, chapter-based narrative format used in Karya Learn's original pilot.
findings: Still in progress — early runs show the pipeline can reliably produce curricula that pass the evaluation agent's own appropriateness and accuracy checks, though it hasn't yet been tested with real learners the way Karya Learn's original hand-written curriculum was.
contribution: I led the project and designed the generation and evaluation prompts — defining what "good" looks like for a financial-literacy story module (audience-appropriate, accurate to the source material, narratively coherent) — building directly on what running Karya Learn's original curriculum had taught me.
